claim.title: Relationship Between Effective Ranks
claim.statement: The two notions of effective rank satisfy \(r_k(\Sigma^2) \le r_k(\Sigma) \le R_k(\Sigma) \le r_k^2(\Sigma)\).
claim.test_plan: Generate random covariance matrices \(\Sigma\) with various eigenvalue decay rates (e.g., exponential, power-law). Compute \(r_k(\Sigma)\), \(R_k(\Sigma)\), and \(r_k(\Sigma^2)\) for several values of \(k\). Verify the inequalities hold numerically.
claim.success_criterion: For all tested \(\Sigma\) and \(k\), the numerical values must satisfy \(r_k(\Sigma^2) \le r_k(\Sigma) \le R_k(\Sigma) \le r_k^2(\Sigma)\) within floating-point precision.

feedback: Prefer a concrete finite-dimensional spectrum for eigenvalue claims (e.g. mu_k = k^-1.5 or explicit geometric decay) at modest n (200-500): the claims are deterministic linear-algebra relations, so a cheap exact computation beats a Monte-Carlo approximation.
